cases.name: c20b
cases.promptMarkdown:
Audit the Solana program in ./program for security issues.

Write your findings to solana-audit-report.md in the current directory. For every finding, write a block with these three lines:

Severity: <Critical|High|Medium|Low|Info>
Location: <path>:<line>
Mechanism: <what is wrong and how it can be abused, in one or two sentences>

Architecture problems count as findings too (for example liveness, centralization or scalability problems), not only bugs in a single line. If you find no issues, write "No findings." in the report.

When you are done, repeat the list of findings in your final message.

graders.name: found
graders.graderMarkdown:
You are grading a security audit report of a Solana program.

The program contains this flaw: `resolve` only checks the `report` against the `reporter` account that the caller passes (`has_one = reporter`) and against the market's `event_id`. It never checks that `reporter` is `market.reporter`. Anyone can create a `Reporter` and a `Report` through `register_reporter`/`post_report`, so an attacker can settle any market with their own result and take the losing pool.

Acceptable places for the finding (paths are relative to the program folder; a report may prefix them with "program/"):
- src/lib.rs lines 172-179
- src/lib.rs lines 78-91
- src/lib.rs lines 13-35
- src/lib.rs lines 120-139
- src/lib.rs lines 230-230

PASS if the report contains a finding that identifies this flaw (the same root cause, not just a nearby symptom or a generic best-practice remark) and ties it to one of the acceptable places, either by a line inside a listed range or by naming the function, instruction or account struct at that place.
The severity of the finding and the section it appears in do not matter.
FAIL otherwise.

Additional guidance: - PASS: the finding says that `resolve` (or its `Resolve` accounts) accepts a reporter or report that is not the one stored in `market.reporter`. Equivalent wordings also pass: "reporter not bound to the market", "missing `address`/`has_one` between market and reporter", "any registered reporter's report can resolve any market". The finding should also give the consequence: an attacker creates their own reporter, posts the result they want, and resolves the market to steal the pool.
- PASS: the finding is framed as "anyone can register as a reporter and resolve markets with their own reports", as long as it says that `resolve` does not compare the reporter or report with the market.
- FAIL: the finding only says that `register_reporter` or `post_report` should be permissioned or admin-only, and does not note the missing binding between the market and the reporter in `resolve`.
- FAIL: generic advice such as "validate oracle/report accounts" or "add more account checks" that does not name the reporter–market relation.
- FAIL: the finding only covers timing (resolving before the event, or reporters posting early) and not the unbound reporter.

graders.name: found
graders.evidence:
# Solana audit report: outcome_pools

Scope: program/src/lib.rs (Anchor 0.31.1). No Solana toolchain was used, so no exploit test was run. The Critical finding was reviewed by an independent verifier and confirmed.

## Findings

### F1
Severity: Critical
Location: program/src/lib.rs:176
Mechanism: `Resolve` never checks that `reporter` equals `market.reporter`. `market.reporter` is stored at line 43 and never read. Anyone can register their own reporter, post a report with the same `event_id` and any result, and call `resolve` right after `closes_at`. That fixes the winner to the attacker's choice, and the attacker then claims the pools.
Verification: confirmed by the finding-verifier. Not run as a test (no toolchain).

### F2
Severity: Medium
Location: program/src/lib.rs:24
Mechanism: `post_report` has no time check, and a report cannot be amended or removed (one report per reporter per event). A reporter can post a result before the event ends, or post a wrong one. `resolve` accepts it from `closes_at`, which is before the event starts, and `winner` is then permanent.

### F3
Severity: Medium
Location: program/src/lib.rs:38
Mechanism: The market creator picks the reporter (line 43), and a creator can use their own reporter. A creator can stake on one side and then settle the market with their own report. Users have no on-chain way to tell a trustworthy reporter from a self-registered one (`register_reporter`, line 14, is permissionless). `closes_at` also has no upper bound, so stakes can be locked for an arbitrarily long time.

### F4
Severity: Low
Location: program/src/lib.rs:162
Mechanism: The ticket PDA is seeded only by market and owner, so each wallet can stake once per market. A second `place_stake` fails because the account already exists. A user cannot top up or hedge on the other side, except by using another wallet.

### F5
Severity: Low
Location: program/src/lib.rs:146
Mechanism: The mint is unrestricted. A mint with a freeze authority can freeze the vault and block all claims. Only the legacy Token program is accepted, so Token-2022 mints are not supported.

### F6
Severity: Info
Location: program/src/lib.rs:186
Mechanism: `claim` requires the owner's signature, so nobody else can settle a ticket for the owner. Funds stay safe, but they can be locked up if a user loses their key. The single reporter per market (line 43) is a liveness dependency. If it never reports, users wait 14 days (line 7) for a refund. There is no way to rotate a reporter's authority.

## Design findings

- Centralization and liveness: settlement depends on a single reporter chosen by the creator (F1, F2, F3).
- There is no dispute or correction path after `resolve` (line 87). Resolution is one-way.

## Coverage

| Item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| root-of-trust | found (F1) |
| role-inversion | found (F2, F3) |
| one-way-state | found (F2) |
| fail-fast | found (F2) |
| dependency-independency | found (F6) |
| untrusted-executor | clear (resolve and claim need no admin; lines 79, 94) |
| boundary-of-consent | n/a (fixed amounts, no computed rate) |
| baseline: arithmetic | clear (checked_add at line 67; u128 math at line 251) |
| baseline: duplicate accounts and closing | clear (ticket closed at line 186 and cannot be reused) |
| other patterns | n/a (no oracle, loops, or randomness) |
